discourses.source_txt: Until the mid-1900s worldwide, the primary objective of special education classes, which were widely adopted, was to ensure that students with disabilities received education in the same school as their peers, but in separate classrooms with students who had similar types of disabilities. It was believed that, to some extent, these classes enabled the mainstreaming of students with disabilities with their non-disabled peers.
discourses.translated_txt: 1900'lerin ortalarına kadar, dünya çapında yaygın olarak kabul edilen özel eğitim sınıflarının temel amacı, engelli öğrencilerin akranlarıyla aynı okulda eğitim almasını sağlamak, ancak benzer engellilik türlerine sahip öğrencilerle ayrı sınıflarda eğitim almasını sağlamaktı.

discourses.source_txt: An example of this can be seen in the case of a 13-year-old student with a physical disability who was transferred from a general education school to a special education school. The reasons cited for this decision included that the student’s physical condition and illness were upsetting and disturbing to the teacher and other students, that the student demanded too much of the teacher’s attention and time, distracted other students, and had a negative impact on discipline and progress at the school (Lewis and Doorlag, 1999).
discourses.translated_txt: Bu kararın alınan nedenleri arasında öğrencinin fiziksel durumunun ve hastalığının öğretmen ve diğer öğrencileri rahatsız etmesi ve rahatsız etmesi, öğrencinin öğretmenin dikkatini ve zamanını çok fazla talep etmesi, diğer öğrencilerin dikkatini dağıtması ve okulda disiplin ve ilerleme üzerinde olumsuz bir etkisi olması yer alıyordu (Lewis ve Doorlag, 1999).

discourses.source_txt: This example is striking in that it reflects the attitudes of society toward individuals who were different at that time.
discourses.translated_txt: Bu örnek, o dönemde farklı olan bireylere karşı toplumun tutumunu yansıttığı için dikkat çekici.

discourses.source_txt: Until the 1900s, due to the lack of adequate special education services in the United States, many students with specific needs were placed in general education classrooms. Students who were placed in general education classrooms without special education support continued their education with the efforts of classroom teachers.
discourses.translated_txt: 1900'lere kadar, Amerika Birleşik Devletleri'nde yeterli özel eğitim hizmetlerinin bulunmaması nedeniyle, özel ihtiyaçları olan birçok öğrenci genel eğitim sınıflarına yerleştirildi. Özel eğitim desteği olmadan genel eğitim sınıflarına yerleştirilen öğrenciler, eğitimlerine sınıf öğretmenlerinin çabalarıyla devam ettiler.

discourses.source_txt: At the end of the educational process, it was decided to remove students who were deemed unlikely to benefit from instruction at present or in the near future, or who were considered to be harmful to other children, from education (Lewis and Doorlag, 1999; Mastropieri and Scruggs, 2000).
discourses.translated_txt: Eğitim sürecinin sonunda, şu anda veya yakın gelecekte öğretimden yararlanamayacağı veya diğer çocuklara zarar verebileceği düşünülen öğrencilerin eğitimden çıkarılması kararlaştırıldı (Lewis ve Doorlag, 1999; Mastropieri ve Scruggs, 2000).

discourses.source_txt: In those years, the concepts of “education” or “care” were discussed more than the debate between “education together” or “separate education.”
discourses.translated_txt: O yıllarda, "eğitim" veya "bakım" kavramları, "birlikte eğitim" veya "ayrı eğitim" arasındaki tartışmalardan daha çok tartışıldı.

discourses.source_txt: Although the prevailing view until the mid-1900s was that students with specific needs should be educated in special education schools, it is noteworthy that, albeit limited, various perspectives and efforts toward mainstreaming also began to emerge during this period.
discourses.translated_txt: 1900'lerin ortalarına kadar yaygın olan görüş, özel ihtiyaçları olan öğrencilerin özel eğitim okullarında eğitilmeleri gerektiği olsa da, sınırlı olsa da, bu dönemde yaygınlaştırmaya yönelik çeşitli bakış açıları ve çabaların ortaya çıkmaya başladığı dikkate değer.

discourses.source_txt: In 1913, it was aimed to mainstream students with their peers in classes—especially in non-academic subjects such as art and music. Additionally, since special education classrooms were designed for students with disabilities in terms of personnel, equipment, physical facilities, and curriculum, it was expected that students would benefit more from these classes. However, the expectation that special education classrooms, prepared for students with disabilities, would lead to greater benefit for these students did not produce the anticipated results in practice. It was first realized that many students with specific needs in these classes did not require full-day special education; on the contrary, they would benefit more from interaction with their non-disabled peers (Lewis and Doorlag, 1999). Furthermore, since special education classrooms were made up of students who were academically similar to one another, it was observed that students with specific needs in these settings did not have access to more successful role models and tended to keep their own expectations low. Similarly, teachers working in these classrooms were seen to have low expectations for these students as well, attributing their lack of learning to the students' disabilities instead of the methods or programs used (Gearheart et al., 1996).
discourses.translated_txt: Özel eğitim sınıfları, personel, ekipman, fiziksel tesisler ve müfredat açısından engelli öğrenciler için tasarlandığından, öğrencilerin bu sınıflardan daha fazla yararlanacağı bekleniyordu. Bununla birlikte, engelli öğrenciler için hazırlanan özel eğitim sınıflarının bu öğrenciler için daha fazla yarar sağlayacağı beklentisi, pratikte beklenen sonuçları vermedi. İlk olarak, bu sınıflarda özel ihtiyaçları olan birçok öğrencinin tam gün özel eğitime ihtiyaç duymadığı fark edildi; aksine, engelli olmayan öğrencileriyle etkileşimden daha fazla yararlanacaklardı (Lewis ve Peelag, 1999). Ayrıca, özel eğitim sınıfları akademik olarak birbirine benzer öğrencilerden oluştuğundan, bu ortamlarda özel ihtiyaçları olan öğrencilerin kendi rol modellerine erişemediği ve bu öğrencilerin çalışma yöntemlerini daha başarılı tutma beklentilerinin düşük olduğu gözlemlendi.

discourses.source_txt: As a result of criticisms in the 1960s regarding the education of students with specific needs in special education schools/classrooms, and various court cases that were brought to trial, mainstreaming practices began to be included in the laws of many countries starting from the 1970s.
discourses.translated_txt: 1960'larda özel eğitim okullarında / sınıflarında özel ihtiyaçları olan öğrencilerin eğitimi ile ilgili eleştirilerin ve yargılanan çeşitli mahkeme davalarının bir sonucu olarak, 1970'lerden itibaren birçok ülkenin yasalarına dahil edilmeye başlanan ana uygulama uygulamaları başladı.

discourses.source_txt: In Italy in 1971, in Norway in 1976, in England in 1974, and in the United States and France in 1975, laws were enacted that made it legally permissible for students with specific needs to receive education together with their peers in general education classrooms (OECD, 1995).
discourses.translated_txt: 1971'de İtalya'da, 1976'da Norveç'te, 1974'te İngiltere'de, 1975'te Amerika Birleşik Devletleri ve Fransa'da, özel ihtiyaçları olan öğrencilerin genel eğitim sınıflarında akranlarıyla birlikte eğitim almalarını yasal olarak izin veren yasalar yürürlüğe girmiştir (OECD, 1995).

discourses.source_txt: Although special education classrooms were initially regarded as beneficial in many respects, it was observed in practice that they did not provide the anticipated advantages; on the contrary, they even brought about numerous problems. Firstly, it was found that, contrary to initial expectations, education in special education classrooms did not result in mainstreaming, even partially.
discourses.translated_txt: Özel eğitim sınıfları başlangıçta birçok açıdan yararlı olarak görülse de, pratikte beklenen avantajları sağlamadıkları, hatta birçok sorun yarattıkları gözlemlendi.

discourses.source_txt: On the contrary, it was observed that special education classrooms in general education schools divided students into two groups—disabled and non-disabled—and that these classes were often placed in the least desirable corners of the school (such as the basement or next to the storage room). It was also noted that special education classrooms separated students with disabilities not only during lessons but also during extracurricular activities. In some schools, recess, meal times, and ceremonies were scheduled at different times for students in the special education class and non-disabled students, in order to prevent negative interactions between the two groups (Lewis and Doorlag, 1999).
discourses.translated_txt: Tam tersine, genel eğitim okullarındaki özel eğitim sınıflarının öğrencileri iki gruba böldüğü ve bu sınıfların genellikle okulun en az arzu edilen köşelerine (temel veya depo odasının yanında) yerleştirildiği gözlemlendi. Ayrıca özel eğitim sınıflarının, sadece dersler sırasında değil, aynı zamanda ders dışı etkinlikler sırasında da engelli öğrencileri ayırdıkları belirlendi. Bazı okullarda, özel eğitim sınıfındaki öğrenciler ve engelli olmayan öğrenciler için iki grup arasındaki olumsuz etkileşimleri önlemek için aralar, yemek saatleri ve törenler farklı zamanlarda planlandı (Lewis ve Doorlag, 1999).

discourses.source_txt: For these reasons, it was observed that special education classes did not result in mainstreaming as intended.

MAINSTREAMING: DEFINITION, DEVELOPMENT, AND PRINCIPLES  
The Education of All Handicapped Children Act (PL 94-142), enacted in the United States in 1975, is a comprehensive law aimed at ensuring that school-aged children with disabilities benefit from appropriate educational services. Several significant decisions regarding the education of individuals with disabilities were made under this law, which was passed in the US.
discourses.translated_txt: İkinci olarak, özel eğitim sınıflarındaki personel, müfredat ve ekipman açısından:  BAŞKAÇIŞ: TAMSİL, DEVELAPLAMA VE KÖNELLER 1975 yılında Amerika Birleşik Devletleri'nde yürürlüğe giren Tüm Engelli Çocukların Eğitim Yasası (PL 94-142) , okul çağındaki engelli çocukların uygun eğitim hizmetlerinden yararlanmasını sağlamak amacıyla kapsamlı bir yasadır.

discourses.source_txt:
Some of these decisions are as follows (Fiscuss and Mandel, 1983; Kırcaali-İftar, 1998; OECD, 1995):

Ending Exclusion from Public School Programs and Services: The law stipulates that every child with a disability of school age has the right to free and appropriate education, and that schools are obligated to accept students with disabilities. It was also decided that the lack of appropriate programs, learning disabilities of the child, or financial difficulties would not be accepted as excuses for denying access. Nondiscriminatory Assessment: It was emphasized that assessment materials and processes must be free from any racial, linguistic, religious, or cultural bias. The adoption of this provision was influenced by instances where children from different cultural or racial backgrounds were misassigned to special education schools. Moreover, the law states that information obtained from a single assessment tool cannot be relied upon. Preparation of an Individualized Education Program (IEP): For every child with a disability who is determined to be eligible for special education services, it was decided that an IEP must be prepared to legally guarantee where, for how long, for what purpose, and by whom the education will be provided.

Education in the Least Restrictive Environment: The law stipulates that students with specific needs should be educated according to the principle of the least restrictive environment. This principle means that the student should be placed in an environment where they can interact as much as possible with their non-disabled peers, while also meeting their educational needs in the best way possible. Arranged from the most to the least restrictive, separate residential/day special education schools are considered the most restrictive educational environment, whereas general education classrooms are considered the least restrictive. When determining the least restrictive environment, the goal is to ensure that the student is together with their peers as much as possible. The least restrictive environment is the setting in which the student can achieve the highest level of success.

Need for Mainstreaming: The law states that students with disabilities require mainstreaming. The placement of a child in a special education school or special education classroom should occur only when, due to the nature or degree of the disability, education in general education classrooms cannot be successfully achieved even with the help of supportive tools and services.

Special Education and Mainstreaming in Turkey  
Today, compared to the past, there have been encouraging developments in the educational opportunities provided for individuals with specific needs in our country.

discourses.source_txt: It is possible to examine these developments, which gained momentum in the 1980s, under the headings of the period up to 1950, the period between 1950 and 1980, the period between 1980 and 1990, and the present period.

discourses.source_txt: Following the enactment of the law in 1975 in the United States, the rights of children with disabilities to benefit from free education in the least restrictive environment, regardless of the type of their disability, were further expanded and highlighted in the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA PL 101-476) adopted in the United States in 1990, and later in the law enacted in 1997 (PL 105-17) (Stainback and Stainback, 1996). In the act passed in 1997, it was stated that the vast majority of students with specific needs should be educated in general education classrooms and that teachers working in these schools should also be recognized as part of the team.
discourses.translated_txt: 1975'te ABD'de yasa yürürlüğe girdikten sonra, engelli çocukların engelliliklerinin türüne bakılmaksızın en az kısıtlayıcı ortamda ücretsiz eğitimden yararlanma hakları, 1990'da ABD'de kabul edilen Engelli Kişilerin Eğitim Yasası'nda (IDEA PL 101-476) ve daha sonra 1997'de yürürlüğe giren yasada (PL 105-17) (Stainback ve Stainback, 1996) daha da genişletildi ve vurgulandı. 1997'de kabul edilen kanunda, özel ihtiyaçları olan öğrencilerin büyük çoğunluğunun genel eğitim sınıflarında eğitim alması ve bu okullarda çalışan öğretmenlerin de ekibin bir parçası olarak tanınması gerektiği belirtildi.

discourses.source_txt: When we look at the period up to the 1950s, the first example we encounter in the education of children with disabilities in our country is the “Enderun School” practice, which is claimed to have been implemented during the Ottoman Empire in the 16th century. Enderun Schools were schools established at that time for the education of gifted children (Ataman, 1984). Regarding the education of individuals who are highly intelligent and gifted, the Idil Biret-Suna Kan Law was adopted during the Republican era in 1948, and thus, the education of the gifted was legally secured (Ataman, 1997).
discourses.translated_txt: 1950'lere kadar olan döneme baktığımızda ülkemizde engelli çocukların eğitiminde karşılaşacağımız ilk örnek, 16. yüzyılda Osmanlı İmparatorluğu döneminde uygulandığı iddia edilen "Enderun Okulu" uygulamasıdır. Enderun Okulları, o zamanlar yetenekli çocukların eğitimi için kurulan okullardı (Ataman, 1984). Çok zeki ve yetenekli bireylerin eğitimi ile ilgili olarak, 1948 yılında Cumhuriyet döneminde Idil Biret-Suna Kan Kanunu kabul edildi ve böylece, yeteneklilerin eğitimi yasal olarak güvence altına alındı (Ataman, 1997).

discourses.source_txt: Another factor that has influenced the adoption of mainstreaming practices today is the acceptance of the concept of “normalization.” This concept first appeared in Danish legislation in the late 1960s and later in legislation in the United States.
discourses.translated_txt: Günümüzde ana uygulama uygulamalarının benimsenmesini etkileyen bir başka faktör de "normalleştirme" kavramının kabul edilmesidir. Bu kavram ilk olarak 1960'ların sonlarında Danimarka mevzuatında ve daha sonra Amerika Birleşik Devletleri'nde mevzuatında ortaya çıktı.

discourses.source_txt: The concept of normalization, which is based on providing individuals with specific needs the opportunity to experience ordinary life, not only advocates for these individuals to be educated in general education classrooms, but also envisions that they will benefit equally from opportunities available to other members of society, such as acquiring a home and job, and participating in recreational activities (Lindsay, 2003; Peterson and Hittie, 2003). With regard to special education, apart from the Enderun practice during the Ottoman Empire, we see that classes for children with hearing and visual impairments were opened in Istanbul in 1889 by Grati Efendi.
discourses.translated_txt: Özel ihtiyaçları olan bireylere sıradan hayatı deneyimleme fırsatı sunmaya dayanan normalleştirme kavramı, bu bireylerin sadece genel eğitim sınıflarında eğitim almasını savunmakla kalmaz, aynı zamanda bir ev ve iş edinmek ve rekreasyon faaliyetlerine katılmak gibi toplumun diğer üyelerinin sahip olduğu fırsatlardan eşit olarak yararlanacaklarını öngörür (Lindsay, 2003; Peterson ve Hittie, 2003). Özel eğitime gelince, Osmanlı İmparatorluğu dönemindeki Enderun uygulamasının yanı sıra, Grati Efendi tarafından 1889'da İstanbul'da işitme ve görme engelli çocuklar için sınıflar açıldığını görüyoruz.

discourses.source_txt: These classes later became a separate school (Akçamete and Kaner, 1999; Özyürek, 2004), and students with hearing and visual impairments received education at this school for a period of 30 years until 1912. After this school was closed in 1912, no developments in the field of special education are mentioned in the relevant sources until 1921.
discourses.translated_txt: Bu sınıflar daha sonra ayrı bir okul haline geldi (Akçamete ve Kaner, 1999; Özyürek, 2004), işitme ve görme engelli öğrenciler bu okulda 1912 yılına kadar 30 yıl boyunca eğitim aldılar. 1912 yılında bu okulun kapatılmasından sonra, ilgili kaynaklarda 1921 yılına kadar özel eğitim alanında hiçbir gelişme söz edilmemektedir.

discourses.source_txt: It is known that during the War of Independence in 1921, a school named the “Private İzmir Institute for the Deaf and Blind” was opened in İzmir, and that this school subsequently operated under the Ministry of Health and Social Assistance until 1950 (Akçamete and Kaner, 1999).
discourses.translated_txt: 1921'de İzmir'de Kişisel İzmir Sağır ve Körler Enstitüsü adlı bir okulun açıldığı, daha sonra bu okulun 1950'ye kadar Sağlık ve Sosyal Yardım Bakanlığı altında çalıştığı bilinmektedir (Akçamete ve Kaner, 1999).

discourses.source_txt: The first systematic effort to train personnel in the field of special education during this period was the establishment of the Special Education Branch within Gazi Education Institute in 1952. Forty students were admitted to the branch, who, after graduation, would provide services for the development of special education in various parts of the country and lead the training of the necessary personnel in this field (Enç, Çağlar and Özsoy, 1987).
discourses.translated_txt: Bu dönemde özel eğitim alanında personel yetiştirmek için yapılan ilk sistematik çaba, 1952 yılında Gazi Eğitim Enstitüsü içinde Özel Eğitim Şubesi'nin kurulmasıydı. Şubeye, mezun olduktan sonra ülkenin çeşitli bölgelerinde özel eğitim geliştirilmesi için hizmet verecek ve bu alanda gerekli personelin eğitimine öncülük edecek kırk öğrenci kabul edildi (Enç, Çağlar ve Özsoy, 1987).

discourses.source_txt: The branch was closed in 1955 after graduating two classes (SPO, 1992).
discourses.translated_txt: Şube, iki sınıfın mezun olmasından sonra 1955'te kapatıldı (SPO, 1992).

discourses.source_txt: With the adoption of the Republic, greater importance was given to education, and views supporting the elimination of gender and class distinctions in education were embraced.
discourses.translated_txt: Cumhuriyetin kabul edilmesiyle birlikte, eğitime daha fazla önem verildi ve eğitimde cinsiyet ve sınıf ayrımlarının ortadan kaldırılmasını destekleyen görüşler benimsendi.

discourses.source_txt: However, the country, which was dealing with problems in many areas at that time, was unable to demonstrate any notable progress in education, and especially in the education of individuals with specific needs.
discourses.translated_txt: Ancak, o zamanlar birçok alanda sorunlarla uğraşan ülke, eğitimde ve özellikle özel ihtiyaçları olan bireylerin eğitiminde kayda değer bir ilerleme gösteremedi.

discourses.source_txt: Until the 1950s, it was believed that children with specific needs were ill and uneducable, and during that period, institutions operating under the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare primarily focused on care (Özyürek, 2004).
discourses.translated_txt: 1950'lere kadar, özel ihtiyaçları olan çocukların hasta ve eğitimsiz olduğu düşünülüyordu ve bu dönemde Sağlık ve Sosyal Yardım Bakanlığı altında çalışan kurumlar öncelikle bakıma odaklanmıştı (Özyürek, 2004).

discourses.source_txt:
Another noteworthy development in the records of 1955 was the establishment of the Psychological Service Center, which laid the foundation for the current Guidance and Research Centers present in all our provinces and which play an important role in the integrated delivery of special education services (Özsoy, 1990). This was followed in 1955 by the opening of special classes for students with intellectual disabilities in two primary schools in Ankara (Yeni Turan and Hıdırlıktepe). These two special classes later became the first examples of the lower special class practice, which is still implemented nationwide today (Özsoy, 1990). We observe that significant developments in the field of special education began to take place starting from the 1950s. One of the most striking developments of this period was the transfer of planning and provision of special education services from the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare to the Ministry of National Education. This transfer of special education services from one ministry to another is important as it indicates a shift in perceiving the issue from being a “health concern” to being considered primarily an “educational matter.”

The years 1956 and 1957 are also important as they mark the enactment of two significant laws in the field of special education. With Law No. 6660, passed in 1956, the scope of the 1948 law was expanded, and measures were adopted to ensure that gifted and talented children would be educated by the state. In 1957, the “Law on Children in Need of Protection” (Law No. 6972) was enacted. Article 22 of this law stated that necessary measures should be taken by the Ministry of National Education for children in need of protection who require special education (Şura Report, 1999).

discourses.source_txt: The most important feature of the 1960s is that the rights of individuals in need of special education were guaranteed by the state in the 1961 Constitution.
discourses.translated_txt: 1960'ların en önemli özelliği, özel eğitime ihtiyacı olan bireylerin haklarının 1961 Anayasası'nda devlet tarafından garanti edilmesidir.

discourses.source_txt: Article 48 states, “everyone has the right to social security,” and Article 50 stipulates, “the state shall take measures to render those in need of special education due to their circumstances beneficial to society.”
discourses.translated_txt: Madde 48'de "herkesin sosyal güvence hakkı" ve Madde 50'de "devlet, özel eğitime ihtiyacı olanların koşulları nedeniyle topluma yararlı hale getirmek için önlemler alacaktır" denir.

discourses.source_txt: Additionally, the 1960s are significant in terms of special education, as they were years in which legal regulations continued and personnel training was carried out within universities.

discourses.source_txt: During this period, Article 12 of the Primary Education and Education Law No. 222, published in 1961, stated that “children who are mentally, physically, emotionally, or socially disabled, even though they are within the age range for compulsory primary education, shall be provided with special education and instruction.” With this provision, the education of children with disabilities within the age of compulsory primary education was legally recognized (Gökçe, Kartal, Rıdvanoğlu, Erezkan, and Alışcı, 2002).
discourses.translated_txt: Bu dönemde, 1961'de yayınlanan 222 sayılı İlkokul ve Eğitim Kanununun 12. maddesi, "Zihinsel, fiziksel, duygusal veya sosyal açıdan engelli olan çocuklara, zorunlu ilkokul eğitimine girme yaş aralığı içinde olmalarına rağmen özel eğitim ve talimat verilir" diye belirtiyordu. discourses.source_txt: Another significant aspect of the 1970s in the field of special education is the "Basic Law of National Education" No. 1739, which was enacted in 1973.

discourses.source_txt: In Article 8 of this law, we see the statement, “special measures shall be taken to educate children in need of special education and protection.” This statement is important in that it demonstrates that special education services are included within the general education system (Gökçe et al., 2002).
discourses.translated_txt: Bu kanunun 8. maddesinde, "özel eğitime ve korumaya muhtaç çocukların eğitimi için özel önlemler alınmalıdır" ifadesine rastlıyoruz. Bu ifade, özel eğitim hizmetlerinin genel eğitim sistemine dahil edildiğini gösterdiği için önemlidir (Gökçe ve diğerleri, 2002).

discourses.source_txt: In summary, when we look at the period from the 1950s to the 1980s, after the Gazi Education Institute, the second significant beginning in the treatment of special education at the university level in Turkey was the establishment of the Department of Special Education within the Faculty of Education at Ankara University in 1965. The Special Education Teaching Program was launched at the Faculty of Education and produced its first graduates in 1987 (Çağlar, 1990). Following the program opened at Anadolu University, in 1986, Teacher Training Programs for the Visually Impaired and the Intellectually Disabled were initiated at the Department of Special Education within the Faculty of Education at Gazi University. Despite these notable developments, it is evident that these advances primarily concerned the provision of education for individuals with specific needs by the state, with most education taking place in special education schools and classrooms and with no systematic effort toward mainstreaming. For this reason, these years stand out as a period in which the number of special education schools and classrooms increased rapidly. The 1980s, however, were years in which significant developments emerged in the field of special education.
discourses.translated_txt: Özetle, 1950'lerden 1980'lere kadar olan döneme baktığımızda, Gazi Eğitim Enstitüsü'nden sonra, Türkiye'de üniversite düzeyinde özel eğitimin tedavisinde ikinci önemli başlangıç, 1965'te Ankara Üniversitesi Eğitim Fakültesi içinde Özel Eğitim Bölümü'nün kurulmasıydı. Özel Eğitim Öğretim Programı Eğitim Fakültesi'nde başlatıldı ve ilk mezunlarını 1987'de üretti (Çağlar, 1990). Bu önemli gelişmelere rağmen, bu gelişmelerin öncelikle özel ihtiyaçları olan bireyler için devlet tarafından eğitim sağlanması ile ilgili olduğu açı

discourses.source_txt: Initially, between 1950 and 1980, special education services were administered by a separate branch directorate under the General Directorate of Primary Education; in 1980, these services were incorporated into the general directorate. With this restructuring, the management of special education services was ensured within the Ministry organization by the general directorate and, at the provincial level, by the Guidance and Research Centers (Akçamete and Kaner, 1999; Şahin, 2003). Thus, a nationwide structure was established for the planning and implementation of special education services.
discourses.translated_txt: Başlangıçta, 1950-1980 yılları arasında, özel eğitim hizmetleri, Başlangıç Eğitim Genel Müdürlüğü altındaki ayrı bir şube müdürlüğü tarafından yönetildi; 1980 yılında, bu hizmetler genel müdürlüğe dahil edildi. Bu yeniden yapılandırma ile, özel eğitim hizmetlerinin yönetimi Bakanlık organizasyonu içinde genel müdürlük tarafından ve il düzeyinde Rehberlik ve Araştırma Merkezleri tarafından sağlandı (Akçamete ve Kaner, 1999; Şahin, 2003). Böylece, özel eğitim hizmetlerinin planlanması ve uygulanması için ülke çapında bir yapı oluşturuldu.

discourses.source_txt: The 1980s were significant not only in terms of personnel training, but also as years during which numerous laws related to special education were enacted and important advances emerged. With the enactment of Law No. 2916 on “Children in Need of Special Education” in 1983, the first steps toward a comprehensive law specific to individuals with specific needs were taken. This law included sections on definitions, principles, institutions and their responsibilities concerning special education, as well as the identification, placement, and monitoring of children in need of special education; and various regulations were issued in accordance with this law (Şura Report, 1999). Law No. 2916 is important because it was the first to address the education of children with specific needs through mainstreaming. In the Fundamental Principles of Special Education stated in Article 4 of the law, it is noted that “necessary measures shall be taken to ensure that children in need of special education, whose situations and characteristics are appropriate, are educated among their non-disabled peers in schools and educational institutions established for the education of non-disabled children.”
discourses.translated_txt: 1980'ler sadece personel eğitimi açısından değil, aynı zamanda özel eğitimle ilgili çok sayıda kanunun yürürlüğe girdiği ve önemli ilerlemelerin ortaya çıktığı yıllar olarak da önemliydi. 1983'te "Özel Eğitime İhtiyacı Olan Çocuklar" Hakkında 2916 sayılı Kanunun yürürlüğe girmesiyle, özel ihtiyaçları olan bireylere özel kapsamlı bir yasa yönünde ilk adımlar atıldı. Bu yasa, özel eğitime ihtiyaç duyan çocukların tanımlanması, yerleştirilmesi ve izlenmesi ile birlikte, özel eğitime ihtiyaç duyan çocukların tanımlanması, yerleştirilmesi ve izlenmesi ile ilgili bölümleri içerdi; ve bu yasa uyarınca çeşitli düzenlemeler yayınlandı (Şura Raporu, 1999). 2916 sayılı Kanun, özel ihtiyaçları olan çocukların eğitimini ana akım yoluyla ele alan ilk yasa olduğu için önemlidir. discourses.source_txt: Again, in the same section, it is stated that "starting special education early is essential" and that "special education services should be based on the needs and characteristics of children." Until 1981, the training of university-level personnel in the field of special education was limited to Ankara University; however, in 1981, a "Special Education Certificate Program" was launched at the Eskişehir Academy of Economic and Administrative Sciences—which later became Anadolu University—and efforts to train personnel on a nationwide scale were initiated.
discourses.translated_txt: Yine aynı bölümde "özel eğitime erken başlamanın gerekli olduğu" ve "özel eğitim hizmetlerinin çocukların ihtiyaç ve özelliklerine göre yapılması gerektiği" belirtiliyor. 1981 yılına kadar özel eğitim alanında üniversite düzeyinde personelin eğitimi Ankara Üniversitesi ile sınırlı kalmıştı; ancak 1981 yılında Eskişehir Ekonomi ve Yönetim Bilimleri Akademisi'nde "Özel Eğitim Sertifika Programı" başlatıldı ve daha sonra Anadolu Üniversitesi'ne dönüşen ve ülke çapında personel yetiştirme çabaları başlatıldı.

discourses.source_txt: Later, in 1983, Anadolu University decided that the education of students should be planned individually, delivered and monitored by experts in the field (Şura Report, 1999). While 75 special education schools were opened between 1950 and 1992, an additional 75 schools were opened between 1992 and 1995, bringing the total number to 150 (Şura Report, 1999).
discourses.translated_txt: Daha sonra, 1983 yılında, Anadolu Üniversitesi, öğrencilerin eğitiminin bireysel olarak planlanıp, alan uzmanları tarafından sunulması ve izlenmesi gerektiğine karar verdi (Şura Raporu, 1999). 1990 yılında yapılan Konsey, ana akımlandırmanın kapsamını genişletme ihtiyacını vurgulasa da, bu yıllarda ayrı yatılı ve gündüz okullarının sayısının arttığı da gözlemlendi. 1950 ve 1992 yılları arasında 75 özel eğitim okulu açılmışken, 1992 ve 1995 yılları arasında 75 ek okul açıldı ve toplam sayıyı 150'e çıkardı (Şura Raporu, 1999).

discourses.source_txt: As seen in the relevant articles, although the integration of students with specific needs is emphasized in Law No. 2916, the phrase "children in need of special education whose circumstances and characteristics are suitable" indicates that mainstreaming is only considered appropriate for some children and remains ambiguous regarding which children are deemed suitable. Furthermore, the absence of a definition of mainstreaming within Law No. 2916 also brings uncertainty as to how this process should be implemented in practice.

discourses.source_txt: One of the most significant developments of the 1990s was the enactment of Decree Law No. 573 in 1997. This decree constitutes the most comprehensive legal regulation concerning children with specific needs in our country. The Decree addresses the principles related to the identification, assessment, and education of children with specific needs, starting from their initial identification. Under the titles of "Identification-Assessment-Placement," "Early Childhood Education," "Preschool Education," "Primary Education," "Secondary Education," "Higher Education," and "Non-Formal Education," the stages of education are defined in the first section of the second part of the Decree.
discourses.translated_txt: 1990'lı yılların en önemli gelişmelerinden biri, 1997'de 573 sayılı Yasa Kararnamesinin yürürlüğe girmesiydi. Bu kararnamede ülkemizde özel ihtiyaçları olan çocuklarla ilgili en kapsamlı yasal düzenleme yapılmıştır. Kararnamede, özel ihtiyaçları olan çocukların ilk tanımlanmasından itibaren belirlenmesi, değerlendirilmesi ve eğitimi ile ilgili ilkeler ele alınmıştır. "Kimlik tespiti-değerlendirme-yerleştirme", "Erken Çocukluk Eğitimi", "Mektep Öncesi Eğitim", "Önsel Eğitim", "İlk Öğretim", "İlk Öğretim", "Yüksek Öğretim" ve "Formal Olmayan Eğitim" başlıkları altında, eğitim aşamaları Kararnamenin ikinci bölümünün ilk bölümünde tanımlanmıştır.

discourses.source_txt: “Special Education Support,” “Assessment,” and “Educational Programs” are also addressed and defined in the same section (MoNE, 2000).

discourses.source_txt: In the second section of the second part of the Decree Law, under the heading "Educational Environments," mainstreaming is defined as the education of individuals with special needs, conducted in accordance with individualized education plans that have been prepared. The 1990s were years in which developments in the field of special education and mainstreaming increased significantly. During this period, both the number of personnel and the volume of research and publications grew.

discourses.source_txt: At the National Education Council, a decision was made to take measures to enable individuals with special needs to benefit more from non-formal education opportunities (Şura Report, 1999).
discourses.translated_txt: Ulusal Eğitim Konseyi'nde, özel ihtiyaçları olan bireylerin, resmi olmayan eğitim fırsatlarından daha fazla yararlanmasını sağlamak için önlemler alınmasına karar verildi (Şura Raporu, 1999).

discourses.source_txt: In line with the decisions of the Council, the 1st Special Education Council was convened in 1991. Commissions were established within this council for different disability groups, and each commission made decisions regarding its own field. One of the important decisions taken was to emphasize day schooling and to expand mainstreaming programs.
discourses.translated_txt: Konsey kararlarına uygun olarak, 1991 yılında 1. Özel Eğitim Konseyi toplandı. Bu konseyin içinde farklı engelli gruplar için komisyonlar kuruldu ve her komisyon kendi alanına ilişkin kararlar aldı. Alınan önemli kararlardan biri, gündüz okulunu vurgulamak ve ana akım programlarını genişletmekti.

discourses.source_txt: In the 1st Special Education Council, mainstreaming was defined as follows: “The education of students with disabilities who are included in mainstreaming programs is carried out together with their peers at all types and levels of schools and institutions, using appropriate methods and techniques” (MoNE, 2000). In this Decree Law, unlike Law No. 2916, the concepts of mainstreaming, individualized education plan, and special education support were addressed. Although the Decree Law is more comprehensive than Law No. 2916, it does not clearly specify where, how, and by whom the addressed concepts will be implemented.
discourses.translated_txt: 1. Bu Kanun Kararnamesinde, 2916 sayılı Kanundan farklı olarak, ana akımlama, bireyselleştirilmiş eğitim planı ve özel eğitim desteği kavramları ele alındı. Kanun Kararnamesi Kanunu, 2916 sayılı Kanundan daha kapsamlı olmasına rağmen, ele alınan kavramların nerede, nasıl ve kim tarafından uygulanacağını açıkça belirtmez.

discourses.source_txt: The Decree bears many similarities to the Education of All Handicapped Children Act, adopted in the United States in 1975. Although mainstreaming practices have been adopted, separate residential/day schools still continue to exist.

discourses.source_txt: According to data from the Ministry of National Education in our country, there are 16 primary schools for students with visual impairments, 47 for those with hearing impairments, and 4 for those with orthopedic impairments; additionally, there are 14 vocational high schools for students with hearing impairments and 2 for those with orthopedic impairments. Moreover, there are 51 vocational training centers for educable children, 77 for trainable children, and 2 for adults with intellectual disabilities.
discourses.translated_txt: Ulusal Eğitim Bakanlığı verilerine göre ülkemizde görme engelli öğrenciler için 16 ilkokul, işitme engelli öğrenciler için 47 ve ortopedik engelli öğrenciler için 4 tane; ayrıca işitme engelli öğrenciler için 14 mesleki lise ve ortopedik engelli öğrenciler için 2 tane.

discourses.source_txt: Accordingly, there are currently 213 separate residential/day special education schools for individuals with disabilities in our country (MoNE, 2004). While the education of many students with disabilities is provided in separate schools, according to information obtained from the Ministry of National Education, the number of students with specific needs included in mainstreaming in 2004 was approximately 49,000.
discourses.translated_txt: Buna göre, ülkemizde şu anda engelli bireyler için 213 ayrı konut/günlük özel eğitim okulu bulunmaktadır (MoNE, 2004).

discourses.source_txt: These figures indicate that although the number of students receiving education in general education classrooms in our country is lower than in other developed countries, there has nonetheless been an increase. Furthermore, considering that there are students with special needs in general education classrooms who have not been identified or formally assessed, it is possible to say that this number is actually even higher.
discourses.translated_txt: Bu rakamlar, ülkemizde genel eğitim sınıflarında eğitim alan öğrencilerin sayısının diğer gelişmiş ülkelere göre daha düşük olmasına rağmen, yine de bir artış olduğunu gösteriyor. Ayrıca, genel eğitim sınıflarında tanımlanmamış veya resmi olarak değerlendirilmemiş özel ihtiyaçları olan öğrencilerin olduğunu göz önünde bulundurduğumuzda, bu sayının aslında daha yüksek olduğunu söylemek mümkündür.

discourses.source_txt: In the Special Education Services Regulation, which came into effect in 2000, special education services to be provided for individuals with specific needs were detailed, starting from the assessment stage and including placement and evaluation services. Mainstreaming was addressed in a separate section, as the seventh part, and its principles and criteria were outlined. In the regulation, mainstreaming is defined as “special education practices based on the principle that individuals with special needs continue their education together with their non-disabled peers in public and private preschool, primary, secondary, and non-formal education institutions, with the provision of support education services.” The regulation states that special education services should be planned according to the educational needs of individuals rather than their disabilities (MoNE, 2000).
discourses.translated_txt: 2000 yılında yürürlüğe giren Özel Eğitim Hizmetleri Yönetmeliğinde, özel ihtiyaçları olan bireylere verilecek özel eğitim hizmetleri, değerlendirme aşamasından başlayarak yerleştirme ve değerlendirme hizmetleri dahil olmak üzere ayrıntılı olarak belirtilmiştir. Ana akış, yedinci bölüm olarak ayrı bir bölümde ele alınmıştır ve ilkeleri ve kriterleri özetlenmiştir. Yönetmeliğinde, ana akış, özel ihtiyaçları olan bireylerin eğitimlerine, özel ve özel okul öncesi, ilk, orta ve resmi olmayan eğitim kurumlarında, eğitim destek hizmetlerinin sağlanması ile birlikte, engelli olmayan akranlarıyla birlikte devam etme ilkesine dayanan özel eğitim uygulamaları olarak tanımlanır. Yönetmelikte, özel eğitim hizmetlerinin, engelli oldukları için değil, bireylerin eğitim ihtiyaçlarına göre planlanması gerektiğini belirtir (MoNE, 2000).

discourses.source_txt: Although the number of students participating in mainstreaming in our country is steadily increasing, the fundamental issue is that no special education support is provided to students with special needs and to teachers in general education classrooms. With such placement, the student with specific needs and the classroom teacher are left to face each other, and the classroom teacher is unable to overcome the problems encountered on their own.
discourses.translated_txt: Ülkemizde ana akımlandırmaya katılan öğrenci sayısı sürekli artsa da, temel sorun, özel ihtiyaçları olan öğrencilere ve genel eğitim sınıflarındaki öğretmenlere özel eğitim desteği verilmemesidir. Böyle bir yerleştirmeyle, özel ihtiyaçları olan öğrenci ve sınıf öğretmeni birbirleriyle yüzleşir ve sınıf öğretmeni karşılaştıkları sorunların üstesinden kendi başlarına gelemez.

Models of Supportive Education in Mainstreaming

Supportive education services within mainstreaming are divided into two categories: in-class and out-of-class support. In-class support education services refer to services provided without removing the student from the classroom environment. In-class supportive education services can be categorized as general education classrooms with consultant assistance, general education classrooms with the assistance of a special education teacher, and general education classrooms with a co-teacher.

General Education Classroom with the Assistance of a Special Education Teacher: In this arrangement, the student with special needs continues his or her education in the general education classroom and receives special education support from a teacher. The special education teacher assists the classroom teacher in matters such as facilitating the adaptation of the student with special needs to the classroom, helping the teacher work with the student, carrying out various activities with non-disabled students, providing direct instruction in the classroom, and fostering positive interactions among students (Lewis and Doorlag, 1999). The amount of time the special education teacher spends in the general education classroom may vary depending on the needs of the student. The advantage of this support service is that the student with special needs does not have to leave the classroom, and the special education teacher provides direct support to the classroom teacher during instruction.

General Education Classroom with Consultant Assistance: In the consultant-assisted general education classroom model, the student with special needs spends the entire school day in the general education classroom and does not receive direct special education support (Lewis and Doorlag, 1999). In this model, the special education consultant provides guidance to the teacher on adapting instruction, managing problem behaviors, and increasing the student’s acceptance in the classroom. Additionally, the consultant advises the teacher on how to adapt or prepare materials according to the student's needs and how to utilize various resources and materials in the classroom.

discourses.source_txt: First and foremost, all school staff—especially the principal—should demonstrate accepting and supportive attitudes toward students with special needs. From the moment of enrollment, children with special needs and their families interact with the principal, vice principal, guidance counselor, other teachers, clerical staff, and other school personnel. The sense of belonging that the student and their family feel toward the school will be influenced not only by the teacher but also by the behavior of these individuals listed above. discourses.source_txt: The classroom environment should be arranged not only to facilitate the learning of students with typical development, but also to support the learning and increase the participation of students with special needs in the classroom and activities. For this reason, the classroom teacher should possess the necessary knowledge and skills not only in terms of having a positive attitude, but also in adapting the physical environment of the classroom, the curriculum, and teaching methods according to different needs, as well as using effective classroom management techniques. If any adaptation is to be made for a student with special needs, the other students should also be informed about this matter. Adaptations may involve arranging the physical environment (such as seating in the front rows), as well as curriculum modifications and assessment adjustments. By informing the students in advance about such adaptations, the teacher will help facilitate the acceptance of their classmate with special needs.

discourses.source_txt: In order for inclusive education to be implemented successfully, both the student with special needs and the teacher in the general education classroom must be provided with supportive special education services tailored to their needs. As previously explained, supportive special education services are divided into two categories: those provided within the classroom and those provided outside the classroom. Resource rooms, itinerant teaching, and special education consultation are among these services.

Daha önce açıklandığı gibi, özel eğitim hizmetleri iki kategoriye ayrılır: sınıf içinde sağlananlar ve sınıf dışında sağlananlar. Kaynak odaları, gezgin öğretim ve özel eğitim danışmanlığı bu hizmetler arasındadır.

discourses.source_txt: Other students in the inclusive classroom should be informed about the student with special needs. They should be given information regarding the emotional, behavioral, and cognitive characteristics of the student with special needs. If the student’s disability has also led to a difference in physical appearance, the teacher should explain the reason for this to the other students. If the student with special needs uses a hearing aid or any kind of prosthesis, the function of this assistive device should be explained to the other students. The explanations given to the students should be accurate and appropriate to their developmental level.
discourses.translated_txt: Özel ihtiyaçları olan öğrencinin duygusal, davranışsal ve bilişsel özellikleri hakkında bilgilendirilmelidir. Eğer öğrencinin engelliliği fiziksel görünümde de bir fark yaratmışsa, öğretmen bunun nedenini diğer öğrencilere açıklamalıdır. Eğer özel ihtiyaçları olan öğrenci işitme cihazı veya herhangi bir protez kullanıyorsa, bu yardımcı cihazın işlevi diğer öğrencilere açıklanmalıdır. discourses.source_txt: In order for inclusive education to provide the expected benefits for students with special needs as well as other students, all parents in the class must cooperate with the classroom teacher. Parents of students with special needs should contribute to their children's development by supporting the skills they acquire at school at home, while other parents should serve as role models for their own children in accepting students with special needs and ensuring peer support in the classroom. The classroom teacher should help to establish and maintain cooperation and positive relationships with parents, and create suitable environments to support this process.
discourses.translated_txt: Özel ihtiyaçları olan öğrencilerin ebeveynleri, evde okulda edindikleri becerileri destekleyerek çocuklarının gelişimine katkıda bulunmalı, diğer ebeveynler ise özel ihtiyaçları olan öğrencileri kabul etmekte ve sınıfta akran desteğini sağlamakta kendi çocukları için rol model olarak hizmet etmelidir. Sınıf öğretmeni, ebeveynlerle işbirliği ve olumlu ilişkiler kurmaya ve sürdürmeye yardımcı olmalı ve bu süreci desteklemek için uygun ortamlar yaratmalıdır.

discourses.source_txt: In a classroom where the teacher complains that the student with special needs takes up too much of their time and tires them out, it will be difficult to achieve the desired level of parental solidarity.
discourses.translated_txt: Özel ihtiyaçları olan öğrencinin çok fazla zamanlarını aldığı ve onları yorduğu için şikayet eden öğretmenin olduğu bir sınıfta, istenen ebeveyn dayanışma seviyesine ulaşmak zor olacaktır.
